description: Serbian-language coverage of the CBK site was confirmed (?lang=sr mirror, Financial Stability Report, board decisions, payment-system oversight) but is thinner in search indexing than Albanian; several sq pages had no sr counterpart surfaced in this pass, and no Serbian-language CBK press-release index was located.

No structured/API or open-data endpoint for CBK statistics was identified. It is unknown whether Seritë Kohore or the krahaso platform expose JSON/CSV endpoints, or whether CBK data is redistributed via IMF/BIS/World Bank aggregators.

Non-bank actors that the CBK register points to — licensed payment institutions, e-money institutions, and the operators of card/ATM/POS infrastructure in Kosovo — were not individually enumerated in this cell, only the register that names them.

The CBK has migrated hosting paths at least twice (legacy /repository/docs/ tree vs current /wp-content/uploads/). Older publications may exist only under the legacy tree and may not be linked from current index pages.
No URL in this slice was fetch-verified; the one fetch attempted returned 403. All liveness assessments are inference from search-engine indexing.
Serbian-language coverage of the bank-own disclosure layer is effectively zero; only the regulator publishes in sr.
Three of ten licensed banks (TEB, PriBank, İŞBANK Kosova) have no confirmed retrievable own-channel report set, including one systemically significant institution.
Disclosure cadence is wildly uneven across the cell: ProCredit and Ziraat publish quarterly, most others only annually, and several archives observed here stop at 2023.
No bank-own press-release / news feed was systematically mapped for this cell; only Raiffeisen's media/lajme section and NLB's ankande-publike were incidentally identified.
The shareholder/general-assembly dimension of workstream A1 has no confirmed public feed anywhere in the cell.
Several candidate URLs here were surfaced through search snippets rather than fetched, and one 2026-dated CBK register PDF path was inferred from a search result title.
No source found that quantifies banking access in Serb-majority municipalities (branch counts, ATM density, card penetration, account ownership) after the 2024 dinar measures and branch closures.
No sr-language POINTER source (link directory, media monitor, curated dossier) covering Kosovo banking/payments was identified; all sr finds are direct institutional or indirect news sources.

Remittances/diaspora transfers into Kosovo — a dominant payment flow — are covered only obliquely; no dedicated corridor-pricing source (e.g. Remittance Prices Worldwide corridor data for Kosovo) was confirmed in this pass.
Payment-scheme and fintech actors (card schemes, PSPs, money-transfer operators licensed by CBK) were not reached in this cell; coverage stopped at banks and regulators.
Cyrillic-script sr sources are under-sampled: only the NBS media Q&A page surfaced in Cyrillic, and searches were run predominantly in Latin script.

Kosovo Customs (Dogana e Kosovës) and the Kosovo Business Registration Agency (ARBK, under MINT) were not searched, though both are government disclosure bodies: customs for cross-border payment and cash-declaration data, ARBK for entity registration and beneficial ownership of PSPs and fintechs.

Serbian-language coverage in this cell rests on one query and on BQK's Serbian mirrors; no Serbian-language search was run against the Assembly (Skupština Republike Kosovo) committee or draft-law pages, nor against the consultation platform's Serbian interface.

No regulatory impact assessment (Vlerësimi i Ndikimit Rregullator / Koncept Dokument) was located specifically for banking or payment-services legislation, although the consultation platform is the designated home for them.

Publication cadence, archive depth and history retention were not established for any of the government sources — unknown how far back consultation records, committee reports or Treasury notices remain retrievable.

Kosovo's access-to-public-documents regime (right-to-information requests to MFPT, ATK, Treasury) was not explored as a collection channel for material not proactively published, such as committee working papers or Treasury banking arrangements.
Neither the BQK register of approved external auditors nor the KKRF register of licensed auditors and audit firms was located at a concrete URL.
PwC and Deloitte Kosovo confirmed with transparency reports; KPMG and EY Kosovo entities unconfirmed.
Bank-hosted auditor reports were confirmed for BKT, BpB, İşbank branch, Raiffeisen and NLB, but not yet for ProCredit Bank Kosovo, TEB, Banka Ekonomike, or the newer entrants.

No central, machine-readable repository of Kosovo corporate audited financial statements (e.g. an ARBK/KKRF filing portal) was identified in this pass, so audited statements must be gathered institution-by-institution.
Albanian-language coverage of this cell is strong; Serbian-language coverage is limited to official bilingual publishers, and no assurance-sector source was found originating in Serbian.

Reform documentation references establishment of an Audit Oversight Board / public-oversight and quality-assurance function, while 2020 Albanian-language press reported KKRF had no inspectors. Current operating status is unclear.

Career pages of several licensed Kosovo banks were not individually located in this pass (NLB Banka, BKT Kosova, Banka Ekonomike, BPB, Banka për Biznes, Ziraat, Credins Kosovo) — only Raiffeisen, ProCredit and TEB were pinned down.

Non-bank payment institutions, e-money institutions and payment-tech vendors operating in Kosovo (e.g. processors, POS/softPOS and core-banking vendors) were not mapped as hiring/sponsorship signal sources; only an incidental vendor mention (core-banking product via a recruiter ad) surfaced.
Serbian-language (sr) coverage of this cell is minimal; no sr-language Kosovo banking event, award or sponsorship channel was identified.
Job postings on Kosovo portals expire and are removed, and event pages are frequently replaced by the next edition; no archival strategy is in place.
Two of the richest weak-signal surfaces — LinkedIn (bank job posts, partnership announcements) and Facebook fintech community pages — are login-walled and ToS-restricted for automated collection.
AKK's decisions register (ak.rks-gov.net/vendimet) was identified but its contents were not enumerated; whether any banking/payments case exists is unresolved.
Only ProCredit, NLB and TEB tariff publications were located. Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, BKT Kosova, Banka Ekonomike, Banka për Biznes, TEB business, Ziraat, and the licensed PSPs/MFIs were not covered.
Court decisions on bank-consumer disputes (Gjykata Themelore/Apelit, and the Kosovo case-law portal) were not searched in this pass.

EU accession/progress reporting and IFI assessments (European Commission Kosovo Report, World Bank/IMF FSAP-style notes) that evaluate consumer protection and competition enforcement in Kosovo's financial sector were not collected.
A machine-readable or standalone BQK complaint-statistics publication (beyond narrative passages inside annual reports) was not found.
Kosovo Banking Association (Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës) not located; also unconfirmed: an insurance/microfinance association (AMIK) and a Kosovo payments/fintech industry body.

Commercial macro/financial data aggregators (CEIC, Haver, Refinitiv, S&P Capital IQ, Moody's Analytics BankFocus/Orbis Bank Focus, Fitch Connect) were not evaluated for Kosovo bank-level coverage this run.

Open statistical data portals were named but not endpoint-mapped: World Bank Global Financial Development Database and WDI, IMF FSI/IFS/CPIS data portals, and ASK's askdata cube API for Kosovo (XK/UVK country codes differ across systems).

No per-bank domain inventory was built for Wayback CDX diffing; without a list of Kosovo commercial bank domains (Raiffeisen, ProCredit, NLB, TEB, BKT, BPB, Banka Ekonomike, Ziraat) the archive recovery layer cannot be operationalised.

Serbian-language coverage was satisfied mainly through CBK's own ?lang=sr translations and one World Bank Serbian PDF; no independent Serbian-language aggregator or archive covering Kosovo's financial sector (e.g. Serbian-language media or NBS-adjacent commentary on north-Kosovo banking) was identified.

No BKT Eurobond / debt-investor disclosure route (prospectus, bondholder report, rating agency reports on BKT and BKT Kosova) was located; BKT is unlisted so debt documentation may be the only investor-grade disclosure with Kosovo detail.
Wiener Börse / OeKB Kapitalmarkt (Austrian statutory storage mechanism for RBI regulated information) was not directly searched, nor was the EU-wide ESAP/OAM route for RBI and ProCredit filings.

ESG/sustainability, Pillar 3 and country-by-country reporting (CRD Art. 89) of the parent groups were not covered. CbCR is exactly the disclosure type that names Kosovo with turnover, profit, tax and employee counts per country.

Earnings-call transcripts and webcast Q&A of NLB and RBI (where management answers analyst questions about Kosovo growth and digital investment) were seen only via a third-party aggregator, not via a primary or systematically collectable channel.

German-language ProCredit disclosure (ad-hoc DE variants, Bundesanzeiger filings) and Slovenian-language NLB disclosure (SEOnet originals) were only lightly touched; both are the legally authoritative language versions.
International card schemes (Visa, Mastercard) have no identified Kosovo-specific disclosure channel.

Processing/switch vendor layer is thinly covered — only Quipu (with Compass Plus TranzWare) is evidenced; other likely vendors (ATM/POS estate operators, personalisation, HSM/switch integrators active in the Western Balkans) are unidentified for Kosovo.
The central bank domain returned 403 to plain fetching, and e-prokurimi is a JS-heavy ASP.NET portal not navigable via web search.
Serbian-language sourcing for Kosovo payment rails currently rests on NBS and Serbian outlets; no Kosovo-institution sr-language payments page confirmed.
No source found that publishes interchange fee levels, scheme fee notices, or merchant service charge benchmarks for Kosovo.

The definitive list of BQK-licensed payment institutions (IP), e-money institutions (IPE) and registered currency-exchange offices (ZKV) was not readable this run due to the 403, so the cell's actor map rests on media-derived names (Paysera Kosova, OneFor, Swinto/Velanis, Numarics, MPAY/KUIK, UFP).
Own-domain URLs for Paysera Kosova, OneFor, Swinto and Numarics were not confirmed in this run; only LinkedIn company pages and media coverage were verified as discovered.
Non-Western-Union MTOs active in Kosovo (MoneyGram, Ria, Small World, Wise, Remitly and bank-hosted remittance products) were not individually mapped; only the Western Union agent UFP was identified.
No sr-language Kosovo payment/remittance source was located; the Serb-majority north's payment channels remain undocumented in this cell.
No financial-statement-level disclosure source exists for this cell: EMIs/PIs in Kosovo publish no annual reports and their filings, if any, were not located.
The e-Prokurimi search interface and the OCDS API have not been exercised; no query pattern, pagination behaviour, rate limits or bot defences are known.

No enumerated list of Kosovo contracting authorities (ministries, ~38 municipalities, central and ~55 local POEs, independent agencies) was assembled, so buyer-side filtering cannot yet be exhaustive.

Serbian-language coverage of Kosovo-government procurement notices is thin — only one sr-language award notice (Tax Administration) and the sr version of BQK procurement rules were found, plus Serbia's own parallel channel.
Structured coverage appears to start around 2020-2021 (OCDS API, Red Flags); pre-2020 municipal and central awards are only partly represented by the Open Data Kosovo dataset.

Award notices give winner and value but usually not full technical specification; the tender dossier and signed contract carry the scope (number of POS terminals, card volumes, SLA) that matters commercially.

Donor- and IFI-funded procurement (World Bank, UNDP, EU/IPA, EBRD, KfW, GIZ) affecting Kosovo payment infrastructure runs entirely outside e-Prokurimi and was only sampled here; EU/IPA and EBRD channels were not searched.
No Serbian-language pointer source was found for donor/IFI disclosure touching Kosovo banking; Kosovo institutional portals publish sr variants but these were not enumerated in this pass.

EBRD and EIB technical-cooperation/consultancy assignments (as opposed to loans) were not systematically enumerated. These TC assignments are where payments-systems advisory and vendor selection actually happen.

Second-tier bilateral and regional funders were not covered in this pass: CEB (Council of Europe Development Bank), Sida, Luxembourg/Austria bilateral facilities, DEG/FMO/Proparco equity in Kosovo banks, and the EU Enlargement/Growth Plan Reform Agenda facility for Kosovo.

Two of the highest-value portals in this cell (IFC disclosure portal, Kosovo e-Prokurimi) are dynamic applications rather than static pages, and TED's high-volume search is best used via API rather than the web UI.

Historical donor-to-bank flows before roughly 2015 were not mapped; only a 2006 KfW case study surfaced. Long-run displacement of donor credit lines by commercial funding is a key structural question for this market.

Card management systems, issuer/acquirer processing and the national card switch for Kosovo have no identified vendor-side source. Which platform processes Kosovo issuers, and whether processing is in-house, group-level (Raiffeisen/NLB/BKT/Ziraat parents) or outsourced regionally, is entirely unresolved.

Serbian-language (sr) vendor disclosure coverage for Kosovo is effectively empty. Only BQK's own sr pages were reached; no sr vendor press release, case study or trade article about Kosovo banking technology was found.

Several Kosovo banks have no vendor attribution at all in this pass — notably Banka Ekonomike, TEB SHA, PriBank (platform vendor, as distinct from IPKO as infrastructure partner) and ProCredit Bank Kosovo (whose app package was not resolved).

Vendor customer-logo walls and gated case-study libraries (ASEE, Temenos, Backbase, Printec, Montran) were not systematically enumerated; several sit behind forms or JavaScript rendering and were not fetched in this pass.

Private-sector bank procurement in Kosovo produces no public tender record, so vendor selection at the eight commercial banks is invisible except when a party chooses to publicise it. Only BQK-side procurement is systematically disclosed.
Zero Serbian-language sources captured for this cell. Local terms tried (privredna komora, članovi, registar) only surfaced Serbia-proper bodies.
Non-bank payment institutions, e-money institutions and card acquirers are not covered by any association found in this cell.
Several key pointers (bankassoc-kos.com, amik.org, ARBK's ASP.NET postback search) are unreachable with plain HTTP collection.
Membership lists were only observed in their current state; no archived member rosters were located, so entry/exit of banks, MFIs and vendors over time cannot be reconstructed.
ARBK bulk/API access exists only through unofficial third parties (micro-devs, applifyer, atlas-studio) of unverified accuracy and continuity.

No per-bank tracking of the sq-language newsroom output about each named Kosovo bank (Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, ProCredit Bank, TEB, NLB Banka, BKT Kosovë, Banka Ekonomike, BPB, Banka Kombëtare Tregtare, Ziraat) — coverage so far is sector-aggregate.
Executive-appointment and board-change reporting (emërime, largime, bordi drejtues) was not specifically probed in this slice.

Social/messaging channels of sq economic outlets (e.g. Buletini Ekonomik on X and Facebook) were seen but not evaluated as collection surfaces; in Kosovo these often carry the release before the website item.
No sq-language archive or paywalled back-catalogue route was identified for older Kosovo banking coverage (pre-2015), and several outlets rotate or renumber article URLs.

Several domains here (kallxo.com, nacionale.com, kosovapress.com, sbunker.org) were identified by brand and appeared in result listings, but their banking sections were not opened, so section paths and current liveness are unconfirmed.
